title: Sovereign Lies: Did Indian governments keep their scheme promises?
summary: The government made a promise when it launched the scheme. Did it keep it? Audits 1,000 SHA-256-pinned Union and State/UT government scheme commitments across all 36 States & UTs and 322 schemes — comparing original statutory/notification launch promises against subsequent tax reversals, benefit cuts, eligibility narrowing, exit restrictions, arrears, or discontinuations, anchored by the Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme.
authority: Union Ministries, Reserve Bank of India, CAG of India, and State/UT Finance & Welfare Departments
statutory_anchors: Income-tax Act 1961 Sec 47(viic) & Income-tax Act 2025 Sec 70(1)(x) (Finance Bill 2026 Clause 35 — SGB)
Constitution of India Arts 112-114, 148-151 & 202-203 (Budgetary, Statutory & CAG Accountability)
Government Securities Act 2006 & Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme Notifications
Finance Acts (2016-2026), Union & State Budgets, CAG Audit Reports & Parliamentary Records
RTI Act 2005 Sec 4(1)(b) & Sec 6(1) (Proactive Disclosure & Public Record Access)
scope: 1,000 real, SHA-256-pinned public scheme commitment checks across the Union of India (500 tasks) and all 36 States & UTs (419 State + 81 UT tasks)

Anchor case Task #1 (p8-union-sgb-anchor-0001): Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme — Finance Bill 2016 Sec 47(viic) redemption tax exemption vs Finance Bill 2026 Clause 35 primary-subscriber-only walk-back, plus all 67/67 SGB tranches
Covers retrospective tax reversals, mid-stream benefit cuts, premature discontinuations, eligibility narrowing, lock-in/exit restrictions, and documented unfunded arrears
Includes 119 verified grandfathered/honored benchmark tasks published as Cleared with equal standing
out_of_scope: Informal political speeches or manifesto pledges lacking official Budget, Gazette, RBI, NSE, Parliamentary, or CAG documentary records
Dynamic non-byte-stable web pages whose cryptographic SHA-256 drifts across live fetches
Personal beneficiary identifiers, Aadhaar, PAN, phone numbers, or personal emails (scrubbed per DPDP Act 2023)

sovereign_lies.scheme_name: Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme — Capital Gains Tax Exemption on Redemption
sovereign_lies.tranche_or_phase: All Active Tranches (2015-16 Series I to 2023-24 Series IV) — Sec 47(viic) / Sec 70(1)(x)
sovereign_lies.authority: Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) & Reserve Bank of India
sovereign_lies.promise_summary: Finance Bill 2016 (Clause 28 inserting Section 47(viic) of the Income-tax Act, 1961) and subsequent Ministry of Finance parliamentary replies (LS Starred Q 295, 2021) exempted capital gains arising on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by any individual, while confirming SGBs are tradable on the secondary market without restricting the redemption tax exemption to primary-issue subscribers.
sovereign_lies.promise_document_ref: Finance Bill, 2016 (Clause 28 — Section 47(viic)) & LS Starred Q 295 (09 Aug 2021)
sovereign_lies.walkback_summary: Finance Bill, 2026 (Clause 35 amending Section 70(1)(x) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, effective 1 April 2026) narrowed the capital gains tax exemption on SGB redemption exclusively to individuals who subscribed at the time of original issue and held continuously until redemption on maturity, revoking tax-free maturity redemption for existing secondary-market SGB holders across all series.
sovereign_lies.walkback_document_ref: Finance Bill, 2026 (Clause 35 — Section 70(1)(x)) & Memorandum Explaining Provisions (p. 65)
walkback_evidence_tokens: from the date of original issue till maturity
Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, 2015 or any subsequent Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme
sovereign_lies.promised_metric: 0% LTCG tax on maturity redemption for any individual holder (primary or secondary)
sovereign_lies.revised_metric: 0% LTCG restricted to original subscribers held continuously till maturity; secondary buyers taxed from 1 Apr 2026
sovereign_lies.affected_group: Individual secondary-market SGB investors across 46 unmatured tranches (130 tonnes outstanding as on Mar 2025)
sovereign_lies.exposure_basis: Issue-price outstanding SGB stock ₹67,322 crore (130 tonnes) as on 20 Mar 2025 per RS Unstarred Q 3434
sovereign_lies.statutory_anchor: Income-tax Act 1961 Sec 47(viic) / Income-tax Act 2025 Sec 70(1)(x); Finance Bill 2026 Clause 35
sovereign_lies.benign_explanation_context: Memorandum to Finance Bill 2026 states the amendment aligns the exemption with its intended scope and ensures uniform application across all RBI-issued SGB series under sovereign parliamentary tax authority.
